overview: Report (1931): Taiwan's Railway Department weighs feeder bus routes, buying out competing bus companies, and expanding motor railcars, predicting sales openings for American manufacturers.

people.name: Charles E. Reed II
variants: Vice Consul Charles E. Reed II

subfiles.title: Report on increasing Taiwan Railway Department revenue
subfiles.from: Vice Consul Charles E. Reed II, Taihoku
subfiles.to: U.S. Department of State; copy to the Consulate General, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The report assesses plans to increase railway revenue through feeder buses, the acquisition of competing bus companies, and expanded motor-operated light railway-car services.
subfiles.summary: Reed reports Taiwan's Railway Department, facing declining revenue, considers feeder buses, buying rival bus lines, and expanding motor railcars, expecting sales opportunities for American manufacturers.

interest: Shows Taiwan's railway department countering bus competition through feeder routes and motor railcars.
